name: Add encrypted-in-repo secrets for infra
description:
Resolve secret 'x/y' calls in infra.luau the same way everywhere (Windows, Linux, CI, offline) with no external service or binary.

Store: .repo-infra/secrets.yaml, committed. Readable names, encrypted values:
  recipients: { <name>: <public key> }
  secrets:    { <name>: <encrypted> }
- Each value: AES-GCM under a data key; the data key is wrapped per recipient with ECDH P-256 + HKDF. Built-in System.Security.Cryptography only (no sops/age/native libs).
- One key per machine: ~/.config/repo-infra/key (OS keychain later); CI reads REPO_INFRA_KEY. Each person and CI pipeline is a recipient.

Resolution order for secret 'x/y':
1. Env override INFRA_SECRET_X_Y.
2. The encrypted file.
3. Missing: plan fails listing every missing secret with the command to set it.
Luau syntax unchanged. Values from provider APIs (managed DB connection strings) never touch the file.

Commands:
  infra secrets init                      create key + file, add self as recipient
  infra secrets set <name>                value from prompt or stdin, never argv
  infra secrets generate <name> [--length 32]
  infra secrets list                      names + who can decrypt, never values
  infra secrets show <name>               explicit reveal
  infra secrets recipients add <name> <pubkey> / remove <name>

Rules:
- apply never writes to the repo; generated secrets are created by generate and committed by the user.
- recipients remove re-wraps data keys, then lists every secret that recipient could read as needing rotation.
- On hosts: secrets go to a separate .env next to the compose file (0600, root), never into compose YAML; plans compare hashes, values never printed or logged.
- External managers (1Password, Vault, cloud) can be added later as extra sources (e.g. op://), not as the foundation.
author: cbk <cbk@snappy.no>

comments.author: cbk <cbk@snappy.no>
comments.text: Design update: with --env, secret 'x/y' resolves '<env>/x/y' before 'x/y' (env override INFRA_SECRET_X_Y still first). Hosts may set become_password = secret 'hosts/<name>/sudo'; when absent the password is prompted once per host before apply starts, passed to sudo -S over stdin, never argv or logs; no TTY or --yes fails the plan naming the secret. Milestone 3 of docs infra-cli/plan.
